correctness.rationale: A maximal input has singleton successor cone and must map to the maximal level. A lower input mapping to a lower point forces surjectivity/permutation of the entire upper level, whereas a lower input mapping upward forces a constant upper map. For at least two upper points, these exclude one another; for exactly one, all lower choices are free. The general proofs of all six rank polynomials use exact onto maps, fixed-image idempotent choice, and the matrix-tree rooted-forest determinant. Endomorphism algebra images have cardinality 2 raised to the size of the dual map image. The script independently exhausts 246606 functions on 15 shapes, tests 9514 bounded functions, verifies modal preservation on all 826 functions through four points, and checks 444 identities. These are finite checks supplementing general arguments.

value.rationale: The class is the smallest nontrivial complete two-level S4 sum-frame family and offers a clean test of the semantic difference between arbitrary finite Alexandrov-continuous maps and modal bounded maps. A one-point change in the upper level changes the entire endomorphism monoid normal form. The classification solves three different natural image-distribution questions for arbitrary family parameters and precisely identifies bounded retraction supports. The stable-image distribution requires an additional functional-digraph/forest argument and is not recovered from the one-step count. The example illustrates distinct ranks within a standard 32-element modal algebra rather than relying on an isolated finite numerical observation.
